title: Two-Browser Convergence Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Analytics
LRS-Lite
Sync
Distributed Systems
description: Run the Chromebook and home-laptop scenario under a last-writer-wins merge and an append-only event-set merge, and identify which of the seven attempts each approach loses.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Convergent sync of LRS-Lite records across browsers
learningObjectives: The learner will compare a last-writer-wins merge with an append-only event-set merge by running the Chromebook and laptop scenario and identifying which attempts each approach loses.
prerequisites: Event identity, version vectors and Hybrid Logical Clocks (Chapter 23)
Why attempt order matters for mastery estimates (Chapter 18)

accessibility.notes: Native p5 DOM buttons, checkbox and radio; describe() summarizes the layout; correctness is shown by check and cross symbols as well as color; text is at least 14 px.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Run the same scenario under two rules and compare outcomes
keyQuestions: How many of the seven attempts does each device count under each rule?
Which attempts does last writer wins lose, and why those?
Why does set union converge in any sync order?
commonMisconceptions: That identical summaries mean nothing was lost
That the newest wall-clock write is always the most complete record
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the lost attempts for a given sync order
Explain the roles of id, version vector and HLC

simulation.modelType: discrete replication model with two merge rules
equations: union: local = local UNION pulled segments, sorted by HLC
LWW: keep the snapshot with the newest HLC stamp; replace the other wholesale
assumptions: HLC values and statement ids are illustrative
Each answer batch is sealed into one segment (seq 1 per device)
Changing the merge rule resets the lab
limitations: Checkpoints, head.json, 412 collisions and Web Locks are not modelled
